# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-361 round 2 @ `1149d1c`, TIER 1) | **NO GO on a BLOCKER its own commissioner did not think to ask for — and it proved the gate's NEGATIVE CONTROL was one boot too narrow** (2026-09-07 17:41) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The best single finding of the day.** It re-derived the builder's four-case table on BOTH heads against real directories — case D driven by a genuine `chmod 0500` dir, not a hand-set flag — then found what the table does not name: the sentinel is written on boot 1, `authEnforced` only when setup completes, so **any restart in that window permanently bricks a fresh Marketplace deployment**, measured at the wire (503 on every route including `/api/auth/enforce`, the one route that could unstick it). Control run: an empty volume serves 200. **F-B is the same class again — flipping the sole producer of `dataDirFallbackActive` leaves the suite 20/20 GREEN**, so nothing shipped would notice the fix being removed. Eleven mutations, each clause individually, incl. M12 the semantic revert that changes no call count. **Refused to call the residue unfiled** when `jira-query.sh` returned rc=3 — "cannot distinguish an empty board from no access". **Reported its own two bad probes** (a 403 that was CSRF; a truncated body that hid `volumeWiped`). Named exactly what its sweep does NOT cover. |
| QA agent (fleet, Datasec/NexusAI RD-363 / SEC-07 @ `b0dec96`, TIER 1) | **GO-with-findings + a HARD BLOCK on offer publication — and it REFUTED a standing fleet conclusion in an unprompted addendum** (2026-09-07 17:38) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | Answered the upgrade-path question the builder's fresh-deploy rationale never reached. Then, unprompted and out of scope, killed the day's `actions/checkout@v7` claim: v7.0.1 exists, published 2026-07-20 — **and named the risk correctly as the OPPOSITE one, "the stated diagnosis, if acted on, means DOWNGRADING A WORKING WORKFLOW."** Scoped its own refutation honestly: verified for NexusAI and for the action, explicitly NOT for the sibling repo. Also tightened rather than contradicted the builder's RD-367: "gate not yet invoked is still not the same as gate passed." |
| Datasec/NexusAI agent (s43) | **Corroborated a retraction from repo history better than the API check that produced it — 104 gitleaks-triggering pushes on the v7 pin — and shipped RD-329 with an honest refusal to claim a red-proof** (2026-09-07 17:43) | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | The pin entered `gitleaks.yml` 2026-06-30; main froze 2026-09-01; **104 commits in between, each a trigger — if `@v7` were nonexistent all 104 would have failed at `Set up job`.** Measures the thing, not the registry. Ran Wednesday's disambiguation in the same turn the retraction arrived and confirmed no downgrade ticket exists. **RD-329: found the code has been correct since 2026-04-25, so no code change closes it — the host serves a build older than the fix**; shipped the missing ALLOW-list guard instead and **refused to claim a red-proof that cannot exist for already-correct code.** Adopted first-hand marking in its STATE block (`[measured]` vs `[YOURS, not verified by me]`) — now fleet method. Named the class: *"a check that cannot fail"* and *"a claim whose instrument is unnamed"* as a pair. |
| Secuura/Blockchain agent (s147) | **#890 ROUND 2 @ `4096bdd1a` — three items done, 149→166 green, AND IT REFUTED WEDNESDAY'S FIX INSTRUCTION IN THREE PLACES WITH MEASUREMENTS** | 1 | **1.0** | 1.0 | **The refutation is the score.** Wednesday specified base64url as the F2/F3 fix, asserting it removed the `-` sentinel. # Kam decision sitting — 2026-08-14

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~09:4x — Secuura/Kintsugi: two dev-box calls from s50 (both small)
> **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.
> Rec: unique credentials (one session's work, agent can generate + record properly).
> **(2) Wallet mnemonic backup location.** Agent correctly refused to write into demo's
> Key Vault on its own authority. Rec: NO dev secrets in demo's vault — it is a
> faucet-funded test wallet, cheap to regenerate; backup waits for Kintsugi's own vault
> if ever needed. One word each.
> *(Also pending your hands: the faucet minute — address + steps on the panel.)*

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)
> Stuart posted on KS-601 (08-19 00:58Z, with screenshot): "Founder credits are live
> ($5000) so good to go." **A new grant does not by itself move the existing credit's
> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."
